page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-32 is an Arm-based compute instance provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs on the arm64 architecture and 64 GB of system memory. Its configuration adheres to a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per dedicated virtual core. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data retention and operating system hosting.

By delivering dedicated Arm compute cores paired with a compute-weighted memory density, the c4a-highcpu-32 instance targets compute-intensive workloads that prioritize high CPU throughput over broad memory footprint. Architectures built for the arm64 instruction set frequently yield favorable compute efficiency per core relative to legacy x86 hardware. The absence of local scratch disks also shifts IOPS and bandwidth responsibilities entirely to external storage attachments.

This server type is suitable for compute-heavy parallel workloads, including software compilation, video transcoding, CI/CD automated build pipelines, batch processing jobs, and microservices deployments where thread concurrency is prioritized over large in-memory caches.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-32 is a compute-oriented virtual server built on the arm64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64 GB of system memory. Configured with a 1:2 compute-to-memory density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance focuses on execution environments requiring substantial multi-core computational power without expansive memory allocations. It features zero discrete graphics processors and includes no integrated local storage, depending entirely on remote block volumes for disk storage needs. Additionally, complimentary public IPv4 addressing is not included. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute cycles, delivering qualitative operational efficiency for containerized microservices, high-throughput web serving, automated build and compilation farms, and distributed batch processing pipelines designed for 64-bit Arm architectures.
